findings.quote: the Aetolians had slipped into debt without realizing it themselves, much less anyone else.
findings.problem: ἔλαθον οὐ μόνον ἄλλους, ἀλλὰ καὶ σφᾶς αὐτούς: they escaped notice not only of others but even of themselves. The English reverses the climax ('much less anyone else').
findings.proposed_fix: the Aetolians had fallen deeply into debt without it being noticed, not only by others but even by themselves.

findings.quote: This was the kind of villainy that followed
findings.problem: ἐγένετο περὶ τὴν τοιαύτην κακοπραγμοσύνην: 'was engaged in / occupied with such villainy'. The subject is not in the extract (fragment begins mid-sentence, presumably Philip); the English invents a sequential 'that followed' and smooths the missing subject.
findings.proposed_fix: [...] was engaged in this kind of villainy

units.note: Remainder clean. Subject of opening verb lost in excerpt; do not supply a name without context.

findings.quote: For Philip wished above all either to manage the whole business himself or at least to keep his intentions in these matters from becoming apparent to the Rhodians.
findings.problem: πᾶν γὰρ βουληθῆναι τὸν Φίλιππον ἀναδέξασθαι ἢ καταφανῆ γενέσθαι Ῥοδίοις τὴν ἐν τούτοις αὐτοῦ προαίρεσιν: Philip was willing to take on/undergo anything rather than let his intention in these matters become apparent to the Rhodians. The English invents 'manage the business himself' and turns 'rather than' into 'either...or'.
findings.proposed_fix: For Philip was willing to take on anything rather than let his intentions in these matters become apparent to the Rhodians.

units.note: Lacuna at end correctly marked [...]. Bracketed [καὶ βασιλέα] is an editorial insertion in the Greek; English renders it without flagging, left as is.

findings.quote: After greeting the man, the figure, once he had raised the woman from her seat and embraced her with his arms, would gradually draw him toward her breasts.
findings.problem: καὶ δεξιωσάμενος, ἐπειδὰν ἐκ τῆς καθέδρας ἀνέστησε τὴν γυναῖκα καὶ περιέπτυξε ταῖς χερσί, προσήγετο κατὰ βραχὺ πρὸς τὰ στέρνα: Nabis greets the man, raises the 'woman' (the figure) from her seat, and (she) embraces/is made to embrace the man, then he is drawn gradually to her chest. The English makes the figure the subject, has 'he' raise 'the woman' as if she were a separate person, and makes the woman the one embraced. The object of περιέπτυξε is unexpressed, so who embraces whom is slightly ambiguous, but it is the victim who is drawn to the breast.
findings.proposed_fix: After greeting the man, Nabis would raise the figure from its seat, have it put its arms around him, and gradually draw him toward its breast.

units.note: Greek grammar of subject/object in this sentence is loose; the following sentence (Nabis presses with his hands on the figure's back, victim drawn by mechanism) is acceptable.

findings.quote: because of the prosperity of the Gerrhaeans
findings.problem: διὰ τὴν εὐκαιρίαν τῶν Γερραίων: εὐκαιρία is convenience/advantage (of suitability or opportunity), not prosperity; the land is fitted out with villages and towers 'for the convenience of the Gerrhaeans', who occupy it.
findings.proposed_fix: for the convenience of the Gerrhaeans

units.note: Numbers (500 silver, 1000 frankincense, 200 stacte talents) match.
